content: The FooEquiv between X and Ulift X is named differently depending on Foo. On the one side we have docs#Equiv.ulift, docs#AddEquiv.ulift, docs#MeasurableEquiv.ulift, docs#Homeomorph.ulift, ... The other convention is followed by docs#Ulift.ringEquiv, docs#Ulift.algEquiv and docs#Ulift.moduleEquiv (which should at least be linearEquiv). Which should we adopt as a convention?

/poll Name for "Ulift X is foo-equivalent to X"
FooEquiv.ulift
Ulift.fooEquiv
Only anonymous dot notation to be precise, right? I say this because it would also be conceivable for FooEquiv.ulift to take an existing equiv and lift universes, but I'm not sure it's useful.
I agree, this is potentially confusing. We have docs#RingHom.ulift for example.
Ah right, I should have looked for it before writing!
I prefer ULift.fooEquiv because I see it primarily as a result about ULift, but ULift.downEquiv is even better since it tells us which way the equiv goes

Christian Merten said:

I agree, this is potentially confusing. We have docs#RingHom.ulift for example.

I would argue this should be called RingHom.uliftMap, because it's related to docs#Ulift.map in the same way docs#RingHom.prodMap is related to docs#Prod.map ?
To be clear I don't have a strong preference here, I'd just like us to make a choice.
Yaël, I assume your actual suggestion is Ulift.downFooEquiv ?

There is also docs#equivShrink, docs#Shrink.algEquiv, docs#Shrink.ringEquiv, etc. I would be very happy if these could be aligned one way or another. I constantly keep forgetting the name equivShrink.
(It would also be nice to align the directions.)

/poll How should RingHom.ulift be called ?
RingHom.ulift
RingHom.uliftMap
Ulift.mapRingHom
(Note: this is technically unrelated to the first poll in this thread, though morally related)
